title: Invited: Automatic Hardware/Software Design for High-Speed Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Guided by a Flight Model
problem: Building high-performance computing systems for size, weight, and power (SWaP) constrained autonomous UAVs is challenging as current domain-specific designs optimize individual modules (VIO, depth estimation, planning) independently rather than considering system-level flight performance.
motivation: Autonomous UAVs are increasingly deployed in industry and academia, requiring optimized hardware-software designs that achieve high-speed autonomous flight under strict resource constraints.
method: The system uses a model of how the drone should fly to define a performance target, then an automated tool explores different versions of perception algorithms (the sensor-processing code) and measures how fast each runs. When profiling identifies bottlenecks—the slowest parts—the tool accelerates them by moving critical non-machine-learning operations onto an embedded GPU (a graphics processor on the drone). This top-down approach optimizes the connections between modules and the design within each module together, choosing hardware and software combinations that hit the overall flight performance target.
key_novelty: Instead of designing each flight module separately, the system automatically decides what hardware and software to use by working backward from flight performance goals, guided by a model of how the drone should fly.
contributions: Top-down automatic design framework guided by flight models for UAV system optimization
Representative design spaces for perception algorithms in autonomous flight
Acceleration and profiling of critical non-AI operators on embedded GPU
40-65% flight speed improvements over manual design methods

metrics.speedup: 40% and 65% flight speed improvement vs manual designs

limitations: Limitations of the approach are not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: Automatic co-design framework for high-speed autonomous UAVs
